Hi Jared —

Thanks for the clear list. I’ve outlined the operational workflow below and attached a one-page checklist and a draft confirmation you can drop into your evidence pack. Looping in Marcus (infra/security) for the technical retention details and Monica (CS) for the coordination steps and request intake form.

Summary workflow (high-level):
1) Request Intake: Customer submits standard deletion request form (attached: acme-deletion-request-form.pdf) to privacy@redwood.ai or via the Console > "Data Requests" flow.
2) Triage & Authorization: CS validates request scope (account id, date ranges, example request IDs if provided). For account-level deletes we require admin confirmation from a pre-authorized contact.
3) Execution window: Once authorized, deletion jobs are scheduled. Prompts/outputs are deleted from live object store within 24 hours; inference logs and request metadata are removed from the hot index within 72 hours (subject to jobs queue/backlog).
4) Backups & Snapshots: Daily backups are retained for 30 days by default; deletion flags propagate to backups and snapshots on the next backup cycle. For immediate permanent removal from backups we offer an expedited retention-rewrite option (requires an order and ~7–10 day window to rewrite archived storage).
5) KV cache and in-memory artifacts: These are ephemeral — no long-term storage; any persisted cache shards are included in the log deletion job.
6) Audit & Confirmation: After completion we send a signed confirmation email and provide a machine-readable audit event (JSON) with deletion job id, affected object keys, and timestamps. We also post an entry to your account’s audit log (Console link).

Deliverables attached: redwood-deletion-checklist.pdf (process + SLAs) and a sample confirmation email. Marcus — can you add the low-level retention timings and any caveats about logs that might be kept for billing/abuse detection?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(rachel_kim@redwood.ai)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data deletion request: prompts/outputs/logs (Acme POC)

Adding the technical specifics Jared asked for — details you can paste into an audit artifact.

Execution details (technical):
- Scope resolution: Deletion jobs operate at object-key granularity. For prompts/outputs we target S3 keys under s3://redwood-prod/customer/<account-id>/inference/{date}/. The job enumerates keys by prefix and deletes objects.
- Logs & metadata: Request logs (request-id, user-agent, timestamp, response-size) are stored in Parquet in our logs bucket and indexed in a short-term ES cluster for 30 days. Deletion removes Parquet files and issues a tombstone to the index. Index tombstones propagate to the hot index within 72 hours; fully removed from cold storage on the next compaction cycle (up to 30 days).
- KV cache: Long-running KV caches for streaming sessions are not persisted beyond session end. There is no separate durable store for KV snapshots.
- Backups: Nightly backups are immutable for 30 days. We have an expedited rewrite process to rewrite affected backup objects (customer-requested) that takes 7–10 calendar days and requires a signed order.
- Confirmation artifacts: We emit a JSON audit event to your account audit stream and include: deletion_job_id, queued_at_iso, started_at_iso, completed_at_iso, total_objects_deleted, sample_object_keys (first 10), operator (system/service-account), and checksum of a deletion manifest. We also provide a human-readable confirmation email.

Caveats / security notes:
- Billing/metrics aggregate data (counters and aggregated telemetry) are retained for billing reconciliation for up to 90 days; these are not reversible per-request (we store only aggregates, not raw prompts).
- If deletion requests reference data stored in external integrations (e.g., third-party logging), we’ll coordinate the transfer but can’t delete upstream copies without their cooperation.

I can provide a sample JSON audit event on request.

—Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
